metadata.title: TMUA 2016 · Paper 2
metadata.description: Worked steps, progressive hints and reviewed follow-up questions.

matches.rationale: Rewrites a radical quotient as powers before definite integration, retaining negative indices and the subtraction of endpoint values.
Integrates positive and negative powers from a rational derivative, adding the initial-value condition.
Integrates fractional and negative powers between exact endpoints, preserving the sign and subtraction of both antiderivative values.
Expands the numerator and divides term by term by a radical, then differentiates the fractional powers.
Simplifies a radical quotient to a short sum of powers before differentiating.
Uses the same radical-to-power conversion and a derivative with both positive and negative fractional exponents.
Solves a quadratic in an absolute trigonometric value, rejects inadmissible values and counts all angles.
Reduces a trigonometric equation to a quadratic in a squared value, filtering by range and endpoints.
Separates square-root branches and covers the complete transformed angular interval.
Enumerates truth values under a shared statement system, keeping exactly-one constraints consistent.
Checks complete truth-teller configurations rather than treating statements independently.

Both impose exactly one true whole statement and eliminate linked truths. The original evaluates finite labels at one shared integer; the candidate uses containment and implication between universal input rules. It transfers the truth-dependency operation without repeating the integer table.
sharedKnowledge: Both impose exactly one true whole statement and eliminate linked truths. The original evaluates finite labels at one shared integer; the candidate uses containment and implication between universal input rules. It transfers the truth-dependency operation without repeating the integer table.

matches.rationale: Tests proposed counterexamples against both the hypothesis and conclusion.
Checks that a composite number has the required digit pattern before using it to refute the prime claim.
Classifies counterexamples by the true-hypothesis, false-conclusion requirement.
Turns an integral-defined repeated operation into a constant-ratio recurrence before finding a distant term.
Repeated square rooting becomes repeated halving of an exponent, practising the operation-to-sequence step.
sharedKnowledge: translate a repeated operation into a recurrence

matches.rationale: Evaluate the calculus-defined numerical term before recognising and summing the resulting sequence. This isolates the calculus-to-sequence translation; the follow-up uses an arithmetic sum rather than the original geometric operator recurrence.
Uses logarithm substitutions to turn linked base relations into simultaneous algebraic equations.

Names a repeated logarithmic expression as an algebraic unknown, then returns to the original variable using the logarithm definition. This isolates substitution and power conversion without the proof-order layer.
Combines logarithms and common-base powers, isolating the power-law prerequisite of the ordered proof.
Tests which consequences of an inequality hold for all allowed signs and proves a valid square bound.
Tracks order reversals from negative factors and tests inequality conclusions on the correct domain.
Refutes unjustified combinations of simultaneous inequalities using fully permitted points.
A decreasing logarithm reverses order; the proof audit makes the monotonicity condition explicit.

The original compares order under odd/even powers and reciprocals. The follow-up tests the prerequisite sign information lost by squaring in a trigonometric proof; it does not repeat the original sufficient-condition classification.
sharedKnowledge: Retain signs when using even powers
Test transformations across the full permitted domain

matches.rationale: The original distinguishes order-preserving odd powers from sign-losing even powers. The follow-up isolates the principal-root sign issue inside a trigonometric proof, so it is prerequisite practice in sign preservation rather than the same order-comparison task.
sharedKnowledge: Retain sign information through powers and principal roots

matches.rationale: Uses an input reflection and output sign change to transfer an entire polynomial root set.

Prerequisite transfer: apply input and output substitutions in the stated order. The candidate transforms a particular quadratic; the original requires a transformation statement valid for the whole zero set of an arbitrary function.
Recognises identities for reflecting an arbitrary function about a shifted axis. This trains exact input transformations without assuming an unstated graph shape.
sharedKnowledge: input reflections and identities for an arbitrary function

matches.rationale: Expresses an arithmetic-series condition and determines which parameter restrictions are equivalent to it.
Tests necessary and sufficient conditions attached to a sequence property rather than assuming each parameter must have a fixed sign.
Expresses the median of an arithmetic progression and tests its integer conditions. It reinforces exact indexing and parameter constraints rather than the original sum inequality.
Tests the false converse that a divisor of a product must divide one factor, matching the original divisibility trap.

Both audit an integer proof in written order. The original fails to bound a proposed remainder; the follow-up infers equal factors from equal products. The transferable operation is checking that a local inference meets its required conditions, not the same remainder calculation.
sharedKnowledge: Separate a valid algebraic identity from an unjustified inference
Locate the earliest unsupported proof transition

matches.rationale: Audits a purported proof one line at a time to identify the first loss of equivalence.
Checks which maximum/minimum configurations can occur for a polynomial using its ends and turning structure.

Both use stationary heights to decide how many horizontal-axis intersections a polynomial has. The candidate practises this operation on a shifted cubic while testing necessity and sufficiency; it does not reproduce four linked level counts of one quartic.
sharedKnowledge: Both use stationary heights to decide how many horizontal-axis intersections a polynomial has. The candidate practises this operation on a shifted cubic while testing necessity and sufficiency; it does not reproduce four linked level counts of one quartic.

matches.rationale: Uses a specified root gap together with the root sum or discriminant to recover a quadratic coefficient.

Both turn a specified condition on two distinct real quadratic roots into a strict discriminant inequality in the coefficients. The candidate requests a shaded parameter region rather than a bound on root separation.
sharedKnowledge: Both turn a specified condition on two distinct real quadratic roots into a strict discriminant inequality in the coefficients. The candidate requests a shaded parameter region rather than a bound on root separation.

matches.rationale: Rearranges a quadratic real-root condition into the corresponding parameter inequality.

Both use corresponding sides of similar triangles to recover a requested length. The candidate creates its similar triangles using tangent-radius perpendicularity; the original obtains them from parallel sides in a trapezium.
Uses a tangent-radius right triangle to recover a length ratio. This trains identifying the relevant triangle and its lengths rather than a second parallel-line similarity argument.
Bounds the possible input interval before counting intersections of a trigonometric curve and another function.
Uses the monotonic branches of a trigonometric graph and a decreasing curve to count exactly one intersection on each eligible branch.
sharedKnowledge: count crossings on monotone trigonometric branches

matches.rationale: Counts trigonometric and quadratic intersections using ranges, symmetry and a central tangency rather than numerical root finding.

Both distinguish a nonnegative integral of a real square from an ordinary signed integral, retaining the whole integration interval. The original seeks a valid counterexample to an ordering claim; the candidate instead proves forced consequences of a supplied integral identity, including a somewhere sign conclusion.
sharedKnowledge: Both distinguish a nonnegative integral of a real square from an ordinary signed integral, retaining the whole integration interval. The original seeks a valid counterexample to an ordering claim; the candidate instead proves forced consequences of a supplied integral identity, including a somewhere sign conclusion.

matches.rationale: Both ask what an everywhere pointwise condition permits one to conclude about signed integrals on a common interval. The original compares f with f² under a size bound; the candidate compares f with g and adds separate derivative-order claims, which are additional work rather than the shared operation.
sharedKnowledge: Both ask what an everywhere pointwise condition permits one to conclude about signed integrals on a common interval. The original compares f with f² under a size bound; the candidate compares f with g and adds separate derivative-order claims, which are additional work rather than the shared operation.

matches.rationale: Combines quantified conditions on a whole function with a counterexample or guarantee, retaining the full domain.
sharedKnowledge: Combines quantified conditions on a whole function with a counterexample or guarantee, retaining the full domain.

matches.rationale: Translates consecutive integers into an equation and uses complete residue cases to identify the exact permitted integers.
A lowest-terms ratio forces integer divisibility. This practises the integer-feasibility check before enumeration; it does not repeat the polygon-angle equation.

Prerequisite transfer: preserve integer feasibility and divisibility when translating the given constraints. The candidate finds common AP terms by congruence; it does not repeat polygon-angle equations or the original bounded polygon-side enumeration.

review.source: Official question papers and official worked answers; manually reviewed solution steps and candidate knowledge links.
scopeNotes: The cube-elevation reconstruction has no close second example in the released archive. Its three follow-ups explicitly transfer 3D interpretation, diagram constraints and exhaustive case checking; they are not represented as elevation duplicates.
Q16 has a close similar-triangle follow-up and two triangle-length or diagram-decomposition transfers.
Q17 uses sine-graph monotonicity, standard values and range bounds; it does not require differentiating sine or using an unprovided compound-angle identity.
